clue.text: Do bottoms-up act with lobster's quadrille partner

parts.note: to act a part is to turn, as a performer does a turn on stage
in Alice in Wonderland the Lobster Quadrille is danced and sung by the Mock Turtle

explanation.surface: Someone performs a topsy-turvy routine alongside a dancer from a storybook quadrille.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lobster Quadrille is the dance in Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, performed by the Mock Turtle and the Gryphon.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to flip over, ending upside down, which is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Indian helmet on head of Caucasian subject

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, a word from India

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A colonial sun helmet sits on a European's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject under discussion.

clue.text: Classic thing on a hill is an acoustic device

parts.note: res is Latin, a classical language, for thing
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An ancient structure on a hilltop serves to amplify sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' points to Latin, the classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that vibrates in sympathy with sound to amplify it is a resonator.

clue.text: Date of planting Tennyson's dove-haunted elms

definitions.text: Date of planting Tennyson's dove-haunted elms

parts.words: Date of planting Tennyson's dove-haunted elms
parts.note: Tennyson's The Princess has the line about the moan of doves in elms described as ancient beyond memory, so their planting is unrecorded

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the elms of Tennyson's poem were planted.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson wrote of 'The moan of doves in immemorial elms'; such trees were planted at a date beyond recall.
explanation.definitionFit: A date beyond memory is the phrase for a time too long ago to be remembered, as Tennyson's elms are.

clue.text: Gatwick's straight-line race courses ?

parts.note: at Gatwick, the London airport, the straight courses where planes race to take off are the strips of tarmac

explanation.surface: Gatwick has straight racetracks for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: Gatwick is a London airport, though the surface suggests a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport's strips for take-off and landing are long straight tracks where aircraft speed along.

clue.text: Dead men can tell no tales after this drink

definitions.text: Dead men can tell no tales after this drink

parts.words: Dead men can tell no tales after this drink
parts.note: in Greek myth the shades of the dead drank from the river of forgetfulness in Hades and lost all memory of their lives

explanation.surface: A pirate's saying about silencing witnesses, applied to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the underworld river of forgetfulness; its water wipes the dead's memories, so they have no tales to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Water of the river Lethe causes oblivion, so its adjective describes forgetful drink.

clue.text: Celia topped this Charles

parts.note: Celia with its first letter removed leaves Elia, the pen name under which the essayist Charles wrote, so this Charles is the man behind Elia

explanation.surface: A woman named Celia got the better of a man called Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped' looks like 'beat', but means beheaded: Celia loses its C. Essays of Elia were written by the Romantic essayist Charles of that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles who wrote the Essays of Elia shares his surname with a young sheep.

clue.text: A light line on one side of the boat

definitions.text: on one side of the boat

parts.note: a beam is a line of light

explanation.surface: A ray of light falls along one side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to a ship's keel, off to the side.

clue.text: Was wrong to put up a pound on Subeditor

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written upwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
sub means under, and ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone erred by betting a pound on a newspaper subeditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses the pound abbreviation, as the clue is written downwards; 'Subeditor' must be split into Sub, meaning under, and the newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To err clumsily is to make a careless mistake.

clue.text: Grant-aided Union leader

parts.note: General Ulysses S. Grant served the president who led the Union side in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A trade union boss whose body receives financial grants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant-aided' looks like funding, but Grant is the Union general; 'Union' is the North in the American Civil War, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Civil War president led the northern states, with General Grant commanding his armies.

clue.text: Party's door-knocker

parts.note: ... Knock is an old parlour game played at children's parties, where a player knocks at the door to deliver kisses as letters

explanation.surface: Someone knocks at the door of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman's Knock is a British party kissing game; the everyday caller who knocks at doors is the mail carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The mail carrier is the character who knocks at the door in the party game Postman's Knock.

clue.text: Picture about making of ale is forbidden

indicators.note: about means one piece surrounds the other, so the forbidden word goes round the reworked drink

parts.note: tabu is an old spelling of taboo, meaning forbidden

indicators.note: making of suggests the letters of ale are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A picture about brewing beer has been banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making of' rearranges ALE to LEA; 'about' wraps the forbidden word round it. Tabu is the older spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or group arranged like a painting.

clue.text: Mrs Morell, note, is standing for Parliament

parts.note: Candida Morell is the heroine of George Bernard Shaw's play Candida
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note says a married woman is running for a seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Morell is Candida, title character of Shaw's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for Parliament is a hopeful seeking election, a nominee.

clue.text: Intended to make a half turn

indicators.note: turn tells us the word for half is spun round to face the other way

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half, as in demigod

explanation.surface: Someone meant to rotate only partway round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses only the half prefix, which follows the A; 'a half turn' reads naturally as a 180-degree spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intended is aimed at a target, meant or purposed.

clue.text: It's given by army bogged down in retreat

indicators.note: retreat means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
in places the army inside the mire

parts.note: to be bogged down is to be stuck in mud
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Soldiers stuck in a swamp while falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'retreat' work together: the army sits in the mire, then the whole is read backwards. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; datum is Latin for a thing given.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin datum literally means a thing given, a fact taken as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Copy a mild sort of savoirfaire

indicators.note: sort of hints at sorting, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentle imitation of social polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges COPY A MILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoir-faire, knowing how to behave, is the tact and finesse of a skilled envoy.

clue.text: One troubled with heat burns?

indicators.note: troubled suggests disturbance, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A person suffering from the effects of the sun's heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges HEAT BURNS; the whole clue also describes someone who has stayed out in the sun too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in the sunshine is the person most likely to suffer heat burns.

clue.text: Lame way circle supports a bad actor

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means the following pieces sit below the actor

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer
St is short for street, a way
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A clumsy route around a stage supports a poor performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lame is to cripple, done by cutting the tendon behind the knee.

clue.text: Constant, heavenly gatekeeper, admits Eugene

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the gatekeeper's name takes the other name inside it

parts.note: Saint Peter keeps the gates of heaven in Christian tradition
Eugene Aram was an 18th-century schoolmaster and murderer, subject of a poem by Thomas Hood

explanation.surface: Heaven's doorman lets in a man called Eugene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts the murderer's surname inside the saint's name; 'Constant' looks like an adjective but is the mathematical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths a parameter is a quantity held fixed for a given case, a constant.

clue.text: Peter announces himself during half-time with drums

indicators.note: during means one piece is set inside the other
half here asks for the first two of the four letters of the word time

parts.note: Peter Pan introducing himself would say I'm Pan

explanation.surface: A man called Peter introduces himself at the interval, with drums playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes TI from 'time', and 'during' sets Peter Pan's self-introduction, I'm Pan, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums in an orchestra are the timpani.

clue.text: Nude model cold? Remedy

definitions.meaning: a chilly unclothed model would want to put her clothes back on, to dress again
to set right or make amends for a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Putting clothes on again is to dress once more; to remedy a wrong is to make amends for it.

clue.text: A bird so caught in a tree died

parts.note: the lime or linden is a tree
d is the standard abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A bird trapped in a tree has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Birds were once caught by smearing branches with sticky birdlime, so a trapped bird was limed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird stuck fast on birdlime has been trapped by that glue.

clue.text: Cockney mate's feature article

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is a Cockney mate

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Londoner's friend has a distinctive item.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, shortened to china.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang, china plate rhymes with mate, so a pal is one's china.

clue.text: I tend to take time out for lunch in Paris

definitions.text: I tend to take time out for lunch in Paris

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Parisian worker says she usually takes a lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I TEND and TIME. A midinette is a Paris shopgirl, named from midi, noon, when she goes out for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a young Parisian seamstress comes from midi plus dinette, a light noon meal.

clue.text: Happening within one's allotted span

indicators.note: within says we keep only the inside of the span's number, losing its outer letters

parts.note: the Bible gives a man's allotted span as threescore years and ten, that is seventy

explanation.surface: Something occurs during a person's lifetime.
explanation.walkthrough: Psalm 90 gives a life as 'threescore years and ten', seventy; 'within' drops its first and last letters, S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening is an occurrence or incident.

clue.text: A party man with a degree found stolen gold

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of the Liberal party
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A politician with a university degree came upon stolen bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Arabian Nights tale, the woodcutter discovers the forty thieves' cave of treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the Arabian Nights story discovered the thieves' hoard of plunder.

clue.text: Point to the inducement that's stirring up feelings

parts.note: E, for east, is a compass point
a motive is what induces someone to act

explanation.surface: Someone indicates the incentive that arouses passions.
explanation.definitionFit: Language that is emotive arouses strong emotion in the listener.

clue.text: Right ? Yes, first time

indicators.note: first says the word for yes comes before the letter for right

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone checks if they have it right and is told yes, at the first go.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, twelve months.

clue.text: Play's opening eleven days before Shakespeare's

definitions.meaning: the opening performance of a play
Shakespeare's comedy is Twelfth Night, and eleven nights before the twelfth is the first

explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the opening performance; eleven before Shakespeare's Twelfth is the first of the nights.
